comment: Native modules under trainvm/include/trainvm/ that no translation unit in trainvm/src/ reaches, transitively, other than the module's own implementation. scripts/ci_unwired_module_gate.py fails on any such module absent from this list, and on any entry here whose module has since gained a production includer or ceased to exist. This is a countdown, not a configuration: it can only shrink. An entry says the module is unwired *on purpose* — landed ahead of its consumer, or a deliberate test seam — because a fully tested module with no production caller is otherwise indistinguishable from working code, and this repository has shipped four of them.

exclusions.reason: Landed ahead of its consumer. The conversion publication document, its API version constant and its parse/validate path are complete and covered by conversion_publication_tests, but no service, CLI subcommand or authority constructs one yet, so no conversion has ever been published through it. Unfinished, not unwanted — do not resolve this entry by deleting the module.

A deliberate test seam, and the one entry here that is not a countdown. FakeWorker exists to drive dispatch and journal transitions without a real worker process; its only consumer is trainvm/tests/trainvm_tests.cpp and that is correct. It is built into trainvm_core rather than a test target, which is why the graph sees it at all. Removing this entry requires moving the source out of trainvm/src/, not finding it a production caller.

Found by this gate on its first run. Its own header comment calls it the 'Production cache publication/adoption fence', and JournalCacheLeaseAuthority is constructed exactly once in the whole tree, at trainvm/tests/cache_namespace_authority_tests.cpp:958. The ICacheLeaseAuthority interface it implements IS reached from production; this concrete implementation is not, so the production path runs on some other lease authority. Same shape as LinuxCacheEvidencePublisher, which 8ca3f10 closed.

Found by this gate on its first run, and the sibling of the entry above. LinuxImmutableCacheStore is the Linux ICacheArtifactStore with the uid, file-count and byte ceilings, and it is constructed exactly once in the tree, at trainvm/tests/cache_namespace_authority_tests.cpp:727. Nothing under trainvm/src/ ever builds one, so those ceilings have never bounded a real publication.

Unwired by a seam CLAUDE.md already documents. The C++ loader is the half that enumerates a disposition scope and rejects missing paths, but load_file only does so when handed a repository root, and source_disposition_catalog_tests.cpp guards that call behind TRAINVM_LEGACY_SOURCE_ROOT, which is unset in CI. What actually checks the pins in every run is scripts/print_disposition_digests.py --check, which walks only the entries a document lists. So the native catalog reader is reachable from no binary. Closing this means giving the loader a caller, which is the same work as the catalog-completeness card.
